title: Painterly Rendering using Limited Paint Color Palettes

supported_dimensions.finding: Adaptive segmentation and stroke evaluation can maintain sharp object borders while reducing spill across small or thin regions.
Coarse-to-fine stroke placement assigns broad marks before narrower detail marks, making finish level a spatial decision rather than a global quality label.
Candidate evaluation can minimize unnecessary overpainting and preserve contrast at segment boundaries.
Thin and opaque layers require different compositing behavior, so surface treatment should remain materially coherent.

limitations: The study optimizes painterly rendering from input images rather than original character illustration.
Its quality objective includes source reconstruction fidelity and should not be copied as a creativity metric.
The limited-palette setup does not establish universal aesthetic preferences.
Hardware-oriented paint modeling does not directly validate digital line-art conventions.
reuse_note: Reuse only the observable controls: mark scale, border respect, overpaint residue, layer behavior, and localized finish. Do not reuse any named style or work reference.

title: Imaginary Stroke Movement Measurement and Visualization

supported_dimensions.finding: Viewers can externalize a velocity field perceived from static marks, supporting mark speed as an observable response dimension.
Viewers can reconstruct cumulative trace paths from static marks, supporting trajectory continuity as a surface-level variable.
Sequential mark cues can be read as coherent actions even in a static image.
Velocity and trace representations expose whether local marks cooperate as a larger directional field.

limitations: The experiments rely on subjective reconstruction tasks and a limited set of visual materials.
Perceived movement does not by itself establish narrative clarity or preference.
The findings do not prescribe one desirable mark speed or trajectory.
The study does not test current text-to-image systems or subculture illustration specifically.
reuse_note: Abstract authorial touch as repeatable velocity, trajectory, and sequencing choices visible in marks; never convert the study into an artist-name imitation token.

title: A Painterly Rendering Based on Stroke Profile and Database
limitations: The matrix translates rendering and perception research into prompt grammar; most candidate rules are design inferences requiring rendered-image holdouts.
It does not define a universally superior finish level.
It cannot prove intentional authorship from pixels.
It excludes named-style imitation and protected-work reconstruction.
reuse_note: Use as an observable decision system for omission, edge emphasis, mark rhythm, and selective finish; combine only a few compatible candidates per prompt.

mechanisms.statement: Distribute broad, medium, and fine marks by structural importance so detail accumulates toward chosen evidence rather than uniformly.
Align or terminate marks at selected object boundaries while allowing controlled spill only where softness is intentional.
Tie mark width and length to the scale of the form being described, preserving thin or small structures with smaller marks.
Assign hard, soft, and lost edges by focal and material role instead of applying global sharpness.
Make local marks imply compatible speeds and trajectories across a region so the surface reads as a deliberate movement field.
Connect mark orientation across adjacent forms when a shared flow is intended, and interrupt it where separation matters.
Retain visible layer history in chosen areas while preventing repeated coverage from erasing focal contrast.
Vary opacity, drag, breakup, and overlap according to the declared surface or medium behavior.

candidate_definitions.ev_edge_priority_map: Specify one primary edge family, one supporting edge family, and one intentionally suppressed edge family.
candidate_definitions.ev_mark_direction_field: Specify a repeatable sequence of mark lengths or speeds that changes only at a meaningful form transition.
candidate_definitions.ev_finish_density_gradient: Concentrate finish around one semantic focal cue while leaving another region visibly unresolved.
candidate_definitions.ev_boundary_holdout: Protect one fragile silhouette or thin structure from cross-boundary marks while permitting softness elsewhere.
candidate_definitions.ev_stroke_scale_ladder: Assign broad marks to mass, medium marks to plane changes, and fine marks to selected identity evidence.
candidate_definitions.ev_overpaint_history: Preserve a limited trace of earlier decisions as visible overlap, correction, or dry residue.
candidate_definitions.ev_surface_drag_consistency: Declare how a chosen material causes marks to glide, catch, feather, or fragment.
candidate_definitions.ev_lost_found_edge_cycle: Describe a contour that disappears into a shared value and returns at a decisive contrast break.

compatibility: Finish gradient is compatible with focal hierarchy and thumbnail readability.
Mark rhythm is compatible with gesture flow when both share one directional field.
Lost-and-found edges are compatible with atmospheric depth when identity evidence remains elsewhere.
Stroke-scale ladders are compatible with limited palettes because scale can carry hierarchy without extra color.
Overpaint residue is compatible with worn-world storytelling when residue follows material history.
conflicts: Uniform outline weight conflicts with edge-selective sharpness.
Global micro-detail conflicts with finish-density gradients.
Random stroke orientation conflicts with trace-velocity coherence.
Heavy cross-boundary smearing conflicts with fragile silhouette preservation.
Simultaneous use of every surface effect conflicts with material-response consistency.
counterexamples: A flat graphic image may intentionally use equal edge weight and still be effective.
A fully rendered decorative image may use uniform detail as its governing rule.
A clean cel-rendered image may contain almost no visible brush history.
A deliberately chaotic scene may break directional coherence to communicate instability.
A tiny icon may require simplified hard edges rather than lost-and-found contours.
boundaries: Do not infer creator identity or intent from mark appearance alone.
Do not encode living or protected creator names as runtime style tokens.
Do not treat roughness as automatic evidence of authenticity or quality.
Do not prescribe physical-media artifacts when the requested medium is clean vector or cel rendering.
Validate edge and finish evidence at both native scale and thumbnail scale.
format_implications: key_art: Reserve maximum edge contrast and finish for the promise-bearing subject-action junction.
cover: Keep identity evidence intact around crop-safe facial, hand, and signature-prop regions.
card_art: Protect the silhouette from frame overlap while concentrating micro-finish inside the frame-safe core.
vertical_scroll: Change mark density across reveal beats rather than applying one finish level to the full strip.
thumbnail: Ensure the primary hard-edge cluster and broad mark masses remain legible after reduction.
viewer_implications: A controlled finish gradient gives viewers a clear first stop and rewards closer inspection with secondary mark history.
Coherent mark trajectories can make a static surface feel enacted rather than mechanically textured.
Selective omission invites completion while preserved identity evidence prevents confusion.
Materially consistent marks help viewers believe that surfaces belong to the same world.
Visible revision residue can suggest process, but only when it does not obscure the depicted action.

illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_edge_priority_map: A visible ranking in which the focal contour contains the highest local edge contrast, supporting contours are softer, and at least one nonessential contour is lost.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_mark_direction_field: Three or more neighboring mark groups share a legible trajectory or deliberately break at a structural boundary.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_finish_density_gradient: Fine-detail frequency measurably increases toward one declared focal zone and decreases in at least one rest zone.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_boundary_holdout: A thin or small structure remains separable from its surround without a uniform outline around every object.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_stroke_scale_ladder: Broad, medium, and fine mark classes are all visible and assigned to different structural scales.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_overpaint_history: At least one area preserves earlier-layer residue or overlap while the focal feature remains unobscured.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_surface_drag_consistency: Mark breakup, opacity, and termination repeat coherently on surfaces declared to share a material behavior.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_lost_found_edge_cycle: One contour alternates between visible, softened, absent, and recovered segments without losing object identity.

title: Aesthetic preference is related to organized complexity

supported_dimensions.finding: Controlled image manipulations showed preference can favor complexity that is structured rather than complexity as raw item count.
Changes to hierarchy and morphology alter perceived interest and beauty even when broad scene identity is retained.
Images can provide multiple discoverable structures without becoming unorganized clutter.
Novel inserted forms help separate some complexity effects from simple familiarity.

limitations: The stimuli emphasize environmental images rather than subculture illustration.
Preference results do not establish one universal optimum density.
The study does not directly manipulate negative space as an isolated variable.
Survey ratings do not reveal the exact viewing sequence for every image.
reuse_note: Use organized complexity as a design question about hierarchy and discoverable structure, not as a target for maximizing detail count.

title: Measuring visual clutter

supported_dimensions.finding: Local variability in color, orientation, and luminance can predict subjective clutter better than item count alone.
Excess or disorganized information can impair search, recognition, and decision speed.
Clutter can make scene segmentation and target separation more difficult.
Edge density, entropy, and feature congestion capture different aspects of clutter and should not be treated as interchangeable.

limitations: The work targets displays and visual search rather than aesthetic illustration outcomes.
Low clutter is not equivalent to high artistic quality.
The measures do not encode narrative importance or genre literacy.
A deliberately maximalist composition may remain effective through learned structure not captured by generic clutter metrics.
reuse_note: Use clutter dimensions diagnostically to protect focal search and silhouette separation; do not optimize all images toward minimal information.

title: Aesthetic preference for art can be predicted from a mixture of low- and high-level visual features
limitations: The matrix converts correlational and experimental findings into illustration grammar, so spatial prescriptions remain design inferences.
Viewer preference varies and cannot be reduced to a single density score.
Negative space can carry culturally learned meaning not covered by the sources.
The matrix does not validate commercial conversion or long-term attachment.
reuse_note: Use empty and dense regions as alternating attention states; preserve intentional maximalism by organizing rather than automatically removing detail.

mechanisms.statement: Reserve low-variation regions adjacent to important forms so their silhouette and action can be segmented quickly.
Increase edge, texture, or object density toward a chosen discovery zone while decreasing competing variation nearby.
Group multiple details into a readable hierarchy of clusters, subclusters, and repeated relations rather than an even field of items.
Avoid peaking color, orientation, luminance, and edge variability in every region at once; assign different channels to different roles.
Maintain a measurable low-conflict band around identity-critical contours even inside a dense scene.
Use unequal open areas to create direction, anticipation, or tension while preserving overall mass balance.
Separate high-density clusters with visible intervals so viewers can parse them as successive beats.
Reduce the number and granularity of density transitions as output size shrinks, retaining only those visible at the target scale.

candidate_definitions.ev_primary_clearance_band: Protect an identity-critical contour with reduced background conflict rather than a mandatory outline.
candidate_definitions.ev_density_heatmap_gradient: Declare a primary and secondary density peak with a declining path between them.
candidate_definitions.ev_cluster_hierarchy: Organize small details into local clusters that belong to larger scene masses.
candidate_definitions.ev_channel_role_split: Assign color variation, edge variation, and texture variation to different compositional jobs.
candidate_definitions.ev_asymmetric_open_mass: Use an unequal open mass as a directional or emotional force, not empty filler.
candidate_definitions.ev_intercluster_interval: Alternate dense beats with visible rest intervals across the intended viewing path.
candidate_definitions.ev_thumbnail_density_survival: Specify which density relationships must survive at thumbnail, cover, and native inspection sizes.
candidate_definitions.ev_discovery_depth: Place one deliberately low-information region beside the focal form and state what it protects.

compatibility: Rest zones are compatible with dense worldbuilding when clues are clustered elsewhere.
Asymmetric open space is compatible with gaze direction and anticipated off-frame action.
Density gradients are compatible with selective finish and edge hierarchy.
Channel partition is compatible with limited palettes and controlled texture systems.
Discovery depth is compatible with commercial thumbnails because it separates first-read clarity from close-view reward.
conflicts: Uniform micro-detail conflicts with a legible density gradient.
Multiple equal-density focal clusters conflict with fast first-read hierarchy.
High feature congestion directly behind a fragile silhouette conflicts with identity clarity.
Decorative filler in every open area conflicts with intentional negative space.
Thumbnail-only simplification conflicts with native-scale discovery if all secondary evidence is removed.
counterexamples: A maximalist decorative field may intentionally eliminate rest zones while using strong repetition for organization.
A minimalist icon may contain only one density level and still communicate perfectly.
A horror composition may deliberately conceal the subject in clutter to delay recognition.
An ensemble poster may need several comparable density peaks when equality is the narrative claim.
A patterned costume can overlap a patterned background if value or silhouette separation remains strong through another channel.
boundaries: Do not equate empty space with calm; it may signal isolation, scale, suspense, or absence.
Do not treat clutter metrics as aesthetic scores.
Do not delete culturally meaningful detail solely to reduce feature congestion.
Do not require a centered subject or symmetric open space.
Evaluate density at the actual delivery sizes and crop variants.
format_implications: key_art: Use one broad rest mass to amplify the central promise while reserving secondary density for world clues.
cover: Keep title-safe space structurally connected to the composition even when text generation is out of scope.
card_art: Concentrate density inside the frame-safe region and preserve silhouette clearance near borders.
vertical_scroll: Alternate dense reveal panels and low-density pauses to control reading tempo.
thumbnail: Retain one dominant mass contrast and suppress details that merge into feature congestion after reduction.
viewer_implications: A clear density gradient lets viewers understand the subject quickly and choose to explore deeper details.
Organized complexity can support curiosity without imposing a costly search for the main action.
Open space can create anticipation by making absence or off-frame direction perceptually active.
Rest intervals reduce competition and make subsequent detail clusters feel more consequential.
Different viewers may prefer different complexity levels, so the goal is legible organization rather than a universal optimum.

illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_primary_clearance_band: A visibly lower-variation band separates at least half of the primary silhouette from adjacent high-detail regions.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_density_heatmap_gradient: The image contains one dominant density peak, one secondary peak, and at least one low-density rest region.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_cluster_hierarchy: Details form at least two nested scales of grouping instead of being uniformly scattered.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_channel_role_split: The regions with highest color variation and highest edge-orientation variation are not identical unless that overlap is the declared focal device.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_asymmetric_open_mass: One side contains a larger open shape that points toward, frames, or delays access to the subject.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_intercluster_interval: Two dense clusters are separated by a continuous lower-density interval wide enough to remain visible at target size.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_thumbnail_density_survival: After thumbnail reduction, the primary density peak and rest zone remain distinct rather than collapsing into uniform noise.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_discovery_depth: A secondary clue becomes visible at native scale without competing with the first-read subject at thumbnail scale.

title: The effect of incongruous contextual cues on pictorial metaphor processing

supported_dimensions.finding: Visible anomaly cues can trigger early suspicion that an image should be read metaphorically.
Conceptual context is decisive for completing a metaphorical interpretation after the initial perceptual trigger.
Perceptual anomalies are detected before conceptual mappings are resolved.
Combined perceptual and conceptual incongruity produces more fixations and longer viewing than perceptual anomaly alone.

limitations: The experiment uses a small controlled image set and a metaphoricity decision task.
Longer viewing does not automatically mean greater liking or narrative success.
The study addresses single-image metaphor processing rather than motif recurrence across a series.
Cultural and genre literacy may change which contextual cues are understood.
reuse_note: Use a literal anchor, an early perceptual deviation, and a later concept-confirming relation; validate interpretability instead of maximizing obscurity.

title: Grouping by Proximity or Similarity? Competition between the Gestalt Principles in Vision

supported_dimensions.finding: Repeated feature relations can make separated elements read as a group.
Proximity competes with feature similarity and can override an intended motif family when spacing implies another grouping.
Common color produced persuasive grouping effects in the tested displays.
Grouping cues do not simply add; spatial and feature relationships can conflict and change the perceived organization.

limitations: The stimuli are simple colored shapes rather than narrative illustrations.
The study does not test semantic motif meaning or emotional response.
Common shape was weaker than other tested cues under these conditions and should not be generalized universally.
The results do not establish how many motif repetitions are optimal.
reuse_note: Use similarity and proximity to make motif instances perceptually related, then vary state or context to add meaning; test cue conflicts explicitly.

title: Effects of Visual Metaphors on Enhancing the Power of Advertisements
limitations: The matrix combines single-image metaphor research with basic perceptual grouping to infer recurring-motif grammar.
Engagement and creativity findings from context research do not guarantee effectiveness.
Meaning may depend on culture, genre literacy, and surrounding narrative.
The matrix excludes copyrighted emblems, protected character identifiers, and named-work reconstruction.
reuse_note: Encode motifs as changing evidence with a source-target relation, not as decorative keyword repetition; require a literal anchor and a payoff state.

mechanisms.statement: Connect a concrete visible motif source to one declared story or character target through shared relations rather than verbal explanation alone.
Introduce one immediately visible deviation in size, material, placement, or behavior that signals a nonliteral reading.
Provide a later contextual clue that narrows the initial anomaly into a specific interpretable relation.
Repeat a controlled color, orientation, contour fragment, or material behavior so separated instances form a motif family.
Alter one property of each recurrence to record narrative progression rather than copying an identical symbol.
Keep at least one ordinary object, action, or environment relation that lets viewers recover the scene before interpreting the metaphor.
Limit simultaneous unresolved mappings so perceptual novelty does not become conceptual noise.
Place the most transformed motif instance where focal hierarchy or sequence makes it a culmination rather than incidental decoration.

candidate_definitions.ev_motif_family_feature: Bind separated instances using one stable color, contour, orientation, or material behavior.
candidate_definitions.ev_motif_state_sequence: Make each recurrence preserve its family cue while changing one event-relevant property.
candidate_definitions.ev_literal_scene_anchor: Keep one ordinary causal relation that remains understandable before metaphor resolution.
candidate_definitions.ev_early_anomaly: Change one perceptual property of an otherwise ordinary element to trigger a second reading.
candidate_definitions.ev_context_confirmation: Add a separate consequence or environmental clue that confirms the intended mapping without text.
candidate_definitions.ev_grouping_separation: Declare the concrete source motif, the narrative target, and the shared relation that makes the mapping visible.
candidate_definitions.ev_mapping_budget: Restrict the frame to one primary metaphor and at most one supporting motif relation.
candidate_definitions.ev_payoff_transform: Place the most transformed recurrence at the focal consequence or final discovery point.

compatibility: Motif state change is compatible with single-image narrative compression.
A repeated feature family is compatible with color scripting and environmental storytelling.
Perceptual anomaly is compatible with negative space when isolation amplifies the deviation.
Literal anchors are compatible with surreal settings because causality can remain concrete.
Motif payoff is compatible with vertical reveals, covers, and card evolution sequences.
conflicts: Identical decorative repetition conflicts with narrative state change.
Several unrelated symbol families conflict with a bounded metaphor load.
A fully opaque allegory conflicts with literal-anchor retention.
Proximity to unrelated similar shapes can conflict with intended motif grouping.
Explanatory text that states the mapping conflicts with image-first discovery when text is not requested.
counterexamples: A purely decorative pattern may intentionally repeat without semantic transformation.
An abstract image may omit literal anchors and pursue open interpretation.
A comedy image may use an immediately explicit visual comparison with no delayed payoff.
A heraldic or interface symbol may need exact repetition for recognition rather than narrative variation.
A motif may appear only twice when the contrast between states is already unambiguous.
boundaries: Do not use protected logos, emblems, character marks, or signature props as candidate motifs.
Do not assume one symbolic meaning is culturally universal.
Do not label ambiguity as failure when open interpretation is explicitly requested.
Do not treat longer viewing time as proof of liking or effectiveness.
Keep source and target descriptions generic and observable in runtime prompt data.
format_implications: key_art: Show a literal scene anchor and one transformed motif at the promise-bearing focal junction.
cover: Use an early motif instance as framing and reserve the altered instance for the character or conflict focal zone.
card_art: Preserve one family feature across variants while changing state evidence to communicate progression.
vertical_scroll: Introduce, repeat, and transform the motif across separated reveal beats rather than stacking all states in one panel.
thumbnail: Retain the family feature and the strongest anomaly; defer subtle contextual confirmation to native size.
viewer_implications: A visible anomaly can stop the first glance, while contextual confirmation rewards continued inspection.
Repeated features help viewers recognize a designed relation before they articulate its meaning.
State changes turn a motif into evidence of time, cost, or character change rather than ornament.
A literal anchor keeps the image emotionally accessible to viewers without specialist genre knowledge.
Bounded ambiguity can support personal interpretation, but excessive competing mappings raise cognitive effort and weaken recall.

illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_motif_family_feature: At least three motif instances share one visible feature such as contour, color relation, orientation, or material response.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_motif_state_sequence: Each recurrence changes one traceable property so the set can be ordered as before, transition, and consequence.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_literal_scene_anchor: One ordinary actor-action-object or environment relation remains readable without interpreting the motif.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_early_anomaly: One motif instance violates an otherwise stable perceptual rule within the first-read region.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_context_confirmation: A separate contextual clue makes one source-target mapping more plausible than unrelated interpretations.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_grouping_separation: Motif instances remain perceptually related despite spatial separation and do not merge with an unintended nearby group.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_mapping_budget: No more than one primary and one supporting unresolved metaphor compete in a single first-read unit.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_payoff_transform: The focal or final motif instance visibly incorporates the consequence of the depicted event.

title: Activation in human MT/MST by static images with implied motion

supported_dimensions.finding: Static images containing dynamic information engage cortical regions associated with visual motion analysis.
A still composition can carry motion-relevant information without literal animation.
Depicted dynamic cues support an inferred continuation beyond the captured instant.
Motion-sensitive processing is relevant to how viewers interpret dynamic content in a static frame.

limitations: Neural activation does not specify which illustration device is aesthetically best.
The stimulus set and imaging method do not cover current subculture illustration formats.
The study does not isolate gesture, fabric, hair, and particle cues separately.
Activation is not equivalent to conscious comprehension or preference.
reuse_note: Use implied motion as a viewer-response target verified through directional and continuation cues, not as a justification for adding generic speed lines.

title: Large Steps in Cloth Simulation

supported_dimensions.finding: Cloth behavior emerges from interacting internal and external forces rather than arbitrary local bends.
Fixed and constrained points determine where deformation can begin and how it propagates.
Stretch, shear, and bending terms produce different visible responses that should remain coherent across the surface.
Contact and collision constraints alter folds and trajectories, providing visible evidence of environmental interaction.

limitations: The work is a numerical simulation paper, not a study of viewer preference or drawing pedagogy.
Physically accurate simulation is not required for expressive illustration.
The model addresses cloth and cannot directly define hair, smoke, water, or rigid debris behavior.
A single static image cannot expose the full temporal accuracy of a simulation.
reuse_note: Abstract only force anchors, propagation, deformation class, and collision evidence; allow expressive exaggeration while preserving one coherent causal field.

title: Pupil responses to implied motion in figurative and abstract paintings
limitations: The matrix joins perception evidence with cloth mechanics to infer expressive illustration rules.
It does not require physical simulation or claim that realism is superior.
Implied motion varies with individual interpretation and genre convention.
The matrix excludes generic effect-token accumulation without causal evidence.
reuse_note: Build motion from one causal field that passes through body, costume, prop, and environment; deviations must signal material difference, collision, or competing force.

mechanisms.statement: Declare the dominant origin, direction, and continuation of force before assigning local pose or effect details.
Carry the action direction from torso and limbs into held props, hair, clothing, and nearby loose elements.
Offset flexible elements behind the driving motion by an amount consistent with their attachment and stiffness.
Show where fabric, hair, equipment, or environmental material is fixed so deformation radiates from a believable point.
Let tension, folds, compression, or bending propagate away from the force or contact zone rather than appearing as isolated decoration.
Arrange displaced particles or small objects as a diminishing directional trail that records the path of action.
Include one aftereffect such as settling cloth, bent vegetation, disturbed dust, or displaced liquid that proves the event persists beyond the pose.
When two forces compete, expose the conflict through counter-curves, tension points, opposing trails, or compressed contact zones.

candidate_definitions.ev_dominant_force_arrow: Specify one dominant force origin, direction, and expected continuation outside the captured instant.
candidate_definitions.ev_gesture_accessory_chain: Connect torso, limb, prop, and one secondary element through a continuous or deliberately interrupted action arc.
candidate_definitions.ev_material_lag_order: Assign different lag amounts to flexible elements according to attachment distance and stiffness.
candidate_definitions.ev_visible_anchor_point: Name the point that fixes or redirects a flexible surface and show deformation beginning there.
candidate_definitions.ev_deformation_falloff: Describe how tension, folds, bends, or compression change with distance from the contact zone.
candidate_definitions.ev_directional_wake: Use displaced dust, water, foliage, paper, or debris as a tapered record of action direction.
candidate_definitions.ev_aftermath_trace: Leave one persistent consequence in the environment after the body reaches its captured pose.
candidate_definitions.ev_competing_force_node: Make two competing forces legible through a shared tension or compression node.

compatibility: A single force vector is compatible with mark-direction rhythm and diagonal composition.
Material lag is compatible with costume storytelling when garment construction remains visible.
Environmental wakes are compatible with single-image narrative compression because they imply a before-state.
Force conflict is compatible with relationship staging when two actors exert opposing actions.
Recovery traces are compatible with transformation scenes when effects show cost and aftermath.
conflicts: Unrelated hair, cloth, and particle directions conflict with a shared causal field.
Symmetric decorative folds conflict with one-sided acceleration unless symmetry is structurally constrained.
Uniform speed lines around every object conflict with material-specific response.
A prop pointing opposite the body action without a visible counterforce conflicts with gesture continuity.
Particles emitted from no contact, source, or wake conflict with environmental causality.
counterexamples: A ceremonial or iconic pose may intentionally suppress implied motion.
A supernatural scene may use a local force field that opposes gravity if the source and affected region are visible.
Graphic impact symbols may replace material deformation in highly simplified formats.
A calm aftermath image may show only residual displacement and no dynamic body pose.
Abstract flow can prioritize compositional rhythm over literal mechanics when physical causality is not the goal.
boundaries: Do not require strict physical accuracy when expressive exaggeration is declared.
Do not add motion streaks or particles without a visible source or compositional function.
Do not infer speed solely from blur; pose, direction, and consequence must cooperate.
Do not force every secondary element into the same vector when stiffness, attachment, collision, or counterforce explains divergence.
Evaluate whether motion survives in a static thumbnail and whether native-scale details preserve causal coherence.
format_implications: key_art: Choose the instant where the dominant action vector intersects the central conflict or promise.
cover: Keep the gesture chain readable around title-safe space and crop boundaries.
card_art: Contain the main force loop inside the frame while allowing a controlled prop or effect continuation beyond it.
vertical_scroll: Use the scroll direction as one optional continuation vector and place aftermath evidence in the subsequent reveal.
thumbnail: Preserve the body-prop-environment vector as a broad mass pattern; remove small wakes that become noise.
viewer_implications: A coherent force chain lets viewers predict continuation and feel that the image captures a consequential instant.
Material lag and deformation make costume and environment participate in the action instead of decorating it.
Aftermath traces invite viewers to reconstruct what happened before the frame.
Visible counterforces can intensify struggle, resistance, or unstable balance without explanatory text.
Causal motion evidence is more informative than generic effect density and remains useful across realistic and stylized rendering.

illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_dominant_force_arrow: Actor posture, prop direction, and at least one environmental response align with one recoverable origin-to-continuation vector.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_gesture_accessory_chain: A continuous visual arc can be traced from a major body mass through an accessory or prop without an unexplained directional reversal.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_material_lag_order: Attached flexible elements show an ordered lag relative to the driver based on attachment distance or stiffness.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_visible_anchor_point: At least one constrained attachment or contact point visibly explains where deformation begins.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_deformation_falloff: Fold, bend, stretch, or compression intensity decreases or changes systematically with distance from the force zone.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_directional_wake: Loose environmental elements form a tapered or diminishing trail consistent with the implied path.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_aftermath_trace: One environment or material state remains displaced after the primary action moment.
illustration_evidence_definitions.ev_competing_force_node: Opposing vectors meet at a visible tension, compression, or contact node rather than producing unrelated curves.
